elements.quote: This systematic literature review aimed to make a detailed overview on the clinical and functional outcomes and to get insight into the possible superiority of a treatment method for extra-articular distal radius fractures
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit statement of the main objective.

elements.quote: Embase, Medline, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for studies describing treatment results.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources used but does not report when each source was last searched.
The abstract does not specify the methods used to assess risk of bias in the included studies.

elements.quote: Out of 7,054 screened studies, 109 were included in the analysis.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies but does not report the total number of participants.

elements.quote: Overall complication rate ranged from 9% after plaster cast treatment to 18.5% after K-wire fixation. For radiographic outcomes, only volar tilt in the plaster cast group was lower than in the other groups. Apart from better grip strength after volar plating, no clear functional differences were found across treatment groups.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for main outcomes including complications, radiographic outcomes, and functional outcomes.
Although the title indicates a meta-analysis, the abstract does not report the summary estimate and its confidence interval for the main outcomes.

elements.quote: Apart from better grip strength after volar plating, no clear functional differences were found across treatment groups.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect ('better') and which group is favored ('volar plating').
The abstract does not briefly summarize important limitations of the included evidence.

elements.quote: Current literature does not provide uniform evidence to prove superiority of a particular treatment method when looking at complications, re-interventions, and long-term functional outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their implications.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: Current literature does not provide uniform evidence to prove superiority of a particular treatment method when looking at complications, re-interventions, and long-term functional outcomes.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the current state of knowledge (lack of uniform evidence) and uncertainties regarding treatment superiority.

elements.quote: Purpose This systematic literature review aimed to make a detailed overview on the clinical and functional outcomes and to get insight into the possible superiority of a treatment method for extra-articular distal radius fractures.
elements.reason: The abstract explains the importance and need for the review (to gain insight into superiority where literature is not uniform).
No mention of previous systematic reviews or the need for an update in the retrieved evidence.
No proposed mechanism of action for the interventions is described in the retrieved evidence.
No logic model is described in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Purpose This systematic literature review aimed to make a detailed overview on the clinical and functional outcomes and to get insight into the possible superiority of a treatment method for extra-articular distal radius fractures .
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the review's objective to overview outcomes and determine treatment superiority.

elements.quote: Five treatment modalities were compared: plaster cast immobilization, K-wire fixation, volar plating, external fixation, and intramedullary fixation .
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly lists the five treatment modalities being compared, satisfying the requirement to state planned comparisons for an intervention review.

elements.quote: The studies were eligible for inclusion if they met the following criteria: (1) Patients who suffered and were treated for an extra-articular distal radius fracture; (2) age 18 years or older; (3) patients were either treated using a plaster cast, K-wire(s), plate fixation, external fixator, or an intramedullary device; (4) primary data for at least one outcome parameter had to be available.
elements.reason: Specifies population, age, intervention, and data availability, but does not explicitly specify settings, eligible study designs, or follow-up requirements as eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: No language limits were used and any potentially eligible non-English language manuscripts were translated if possible by native speaking colleagues or using Google translate, if no native speaker was available.
elements.reason: Specifies language criteria (no limits), but does not explicitly specify dissemination year or publication/report status criteria.

elements.quote: Studies without a clear description of fracture type or intervention, or studies that lacked sufficient data for analysis were excluded.
elements.reason: The text groups data availability issues together without distinguishing between outcomes not measured versus outcomes not reported.

elements.quote: These 136 cohorts consisted of a total of 6707 patients divided over the five different treatment modalities... All outcome data were pooled for four different follow-up periods: 0-3 months, > 3-6 months, > 6-12 months, and 12 months or longer (long term).
elements.reason: Groups used in synthesis (treatment modalities and follow-up periods) are clearly specified and linked to the review's focus on treatment options.

elements.quote: Studies describing a not-commonly used device or technique for extra-articular fractures were excluded ( i.e. dorsal plates, Epibloc system, cannulated screw, above elbow cast, etc.).
elements.reason: Exclusion criteria are listed, but rationales for these restrictions (e.g., why these devices were considered not commonly used) are not provided.

elements.quote: Heterogeneity testing was performed using Cochran's Q and the I^2 statistic. Q is distributed as a chisquare statistic with k (number of studies) minus 1 degrees of freedom. Q has low power as a comprehensive test of heterogeneity [15]. The I^2 statistic describes the percentage of variation across studies that is due to heterogeneity rather than chance [16, 17]. A random-effects model was used if the I^2 value was larger than 40%. When the I^2 was lower than 40% a fixed-effects model was used.

elements.quote: This systematic review had several limitations. First, most studies that were included were retrospective or prospective observational studies, with disappointing reporting quality for continuous data. For a proper meta-analysis of continuous data the mean, a measure of dispersion (either standard deviation, standard error or confidence interval), and sample size are necessary. Many studies in this review failed to provide these data. Moreover, the number of large, well-designed RCTs on extra-articular fractures is very low, and therefore it is very well possible to have a type 2 error. Second, selection bias in the source studies might have influenced the results of the meta-analysis, since stable and simple extra-articular fractures might have been treated nonoperatively, whereas the more dislocated and comminuted fractures might have been treated by volar plating or external fixator. However, current data did not allow for metaregression analyses. Therefore, it is not entirely certain if the current whether the findings are related to the treatment type, or can be explained by a difference in indication. Third, there was high heterogeneity in type of outcome parameters and time points of measurements reported.
elements.reason: The Discussion section explicitly states 'This systematic review had several limitations' and proceeds to detail issues regarding reporting quality, study design (lack of RCTs), selection bias, and heterogeneity of the included evidence.
